sprites.summary: Track A, measured from rendered frames: the "pixelated" engineer and WOLF on main come from sampling 1024x1536 and 1902x1015 sprites at 6x to 18x minification with mipmaps off. The bilinear filter skips most source texels, so outlines go jagged and break up. The branch's mipmaps (LINEAR_WITH_MIPMAPS) already remove that aliasing, but the characters come out soft and slightly blurry next to the crisper props. The project setting rendering/textures/default_filters/texture_mipmap_bias has no effect in this GL Compatibility 2D renderer: the character pixels are identical with it set to -1. A per-sprite canvas shader LOD bias of -0.5 does sharpen the characters without bringing the aliasing back. Lanczos pre-downscaling to about 2x the 1080p size makes little visible difference on its own. It cuts the three character textures from about 27 MB to about 2.7 MB of VRAM (estimated), and with a bias of -0.5 it comes closest to an offline ideal downscale. The other cause is resolution: at the default 960x540 window, Rowan is only 94 px tall, so no filter can show much detail. A 1280x720 first window makes him 125 px tall. Plate VRAM compression (S3TC, desktop) gives about 37 dB PSNR against lossless with 4x4 block structure in the difference map, but I could not see a difference at 1x to 3x. ETC2 and ASTC on mobile were not rendered. Nobody played these variants by hand, so game feel is not validated.
sprites.findings_markdown:
## Track A — why the engineer and WOLF look pixelated

**Setup (all measured on this machine):** Godot 4.7.2, OpenGL 4.1 Metal Compatibility on an Apple M1 Pro. I used detached worktrees of main `dc383dc` and the branch `934f1b2`, each imported twice headless. A driver script (`audit_frames.gd`) captured the opening, corridor start and relay frames. It also logged where each sprite's opaque bounding box lands on screen, taken from engine transforms. The window sizes were 960x540, 1280x720 and 1920x937. A 1920x937 window is pillarboxed to a 1665x937 content area, because the stretch aspect is "keep". I also rendered offscreen SubViewports at 1920x1080 and 2560x1440, which work with `size_2d_override` 960x540 plus stretch. Captures are stills, and nothing was played by hand.

### Root cause (measured)
- **Main** imports the character PNGs with `mipmaps/generate=false` and the default LINEAR filter. Gameplay zoom is 1.18.
- Rowan's opaque art is 1478 px tall and is drawn 82 px tall at 960x540, which is **18x minification**. At 1920x937 it is 142 px (10.4x). WOLF is 72.6 px (11.6x) and 126 px (6.7x).
- Bilinear sampling without mipmaps reads 4 texels out of hundreds per screen pixel. The crops show stair-stepped, broken outlines and speckle.
- Control test: the branch with only the character filter forced to plain LINEAR (`v2n`) brings back the same jaggies. Mipmaps are what change it, not the new art or the zoom.
- **Branch:** with mipmaps and trilinear filtering the aliasing is gone, but the result is soft. Godot's 2x2 box mipmaps sampled at 9x to 16x land on mip levels 3 to 4.
- The props are sharper, at about 3.4x minification, and are drawn in a pixel-art style. That makes the soft characters stand out more.
- **Resolution floor:** at the default 960x540 window, Rowan is only **94 px** tall and WOLF **83 px**, whatever the filter.

### On-screen size and minification (opaque height in px, ratio = texture px per screen px)
| size | main Rowan | branch Rowan | branch WOLF | Lanczos-art Rowan / WOLF |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 960x540 | 82.0 px, 18.0x | 93.8 px, 15.8x | 82.8 px, 10.1x | 3.9x / 4.0x |
| 1280x720 | 109 px, 13.5x | 125 px, 11.8x | 110 px, 7.6x | 3.0x / 3.0x |
| 1920x937 window | 142 px, 10.4x | 163 px, 9.1x | 144 px, 5.8x | 2.3x / 2.3x |
| 1920x1080 (SubViewport) | 164 px, 9.0x | 188 px, 7.9x | 166 px, 5.1x | 2.0x / 2.0x |
| 2560x1440 (SubViewport) | 219 px, 6.8x | 250 px, 5.9x | 221 px, 3.8x | 1.5x / 1.5x |

The Director in the opening shot (zoom 1.95) is 136 px tall at 10.9x minification at 960x540, and 235 px at 6.3x at 1920x937.

### Variants tested
Gradient energy is the mean absolute neighbour difference over the character crop. Higher means sharper or more aliased, so read it together with the crops.

| variant | 960 Rowan | 1920w Rowan | 2560 Rowan | visual (from the crops) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| v1 main as shipped | 31.9 | 24.5 | 20.1 | jagged, broken outlines (aliasing) |
| v2 branch as committed | 16.9 | 14.4 | 12.8 | clean but soft |
| v3 Lanczos art at about 2x of 1080p (256x384 / 761x406 / 256x384) | 17.4 | 14.9 | 13.6 | about the same as v2 |
| v4 project `texture_mipmap_bias=-1` (override.cfg; read back as -1.0) | 16.9 | 14.4 | 12.8 | **no effect**: character-crop RMSE vs v2 is 0.00 |
| v4s shader LOD bias -1 (`texture(TEXTURE, UV, -1.0)`) | 22.5 | 20.1 | 18.1 | sharp, faint shimmer starting at 960 |
| v4s5 shader bias -0.5 | 19.3 | 17.0 | 15.9 | sharper than v2, no visible aliasing |
| v2n branch, mipmaps off | 34.6 | 28.6 | 23.7 | aliased like main (control) |
| v3n Lanczos art, mipmaps off | 29.8 | 22.7 | 17.6 | crisp at 1920 and up, aliased at 960 |
| v3s Lanczos art + shader bias -0.5 | 19.8 | 17.7 | 17.1 | sharpest clean result, closest to the offline ideal Lanczos reference |

Window size as a fix: a 1280x720 first window makes the characters 33% larger than 960x540 (Rowan 94 to 125 px). A 1920x937 window or a maximised 1080p screen gives 163 to 188 px.

### Director and props
- **Director:** same pattern as the characters (main is aliased, the branch is soft).
- **Props:** at about 3.4x minification with mipmaps, the props look clean in both builds. No blocking was seen.
- **Plates:** the room plates are 1920x1080 drawn at 0.675 world scale with mipmaps off. That is 1.48x minification at 960x540, a mild level, and I saw nothing objectionable.

### VRAM-compressed plates (desktop S3TC) vs lossless
- I compared corridor-start frames, where the camera is identical between runs. The run-to-run noise floor in the left-machinery region is 0.00.
- Compression error there is RMSE 3.44 to 3.87, PSNR 36.4 to 37.4 dB, max 40 to 86 per channel.
- The difference map shows 4x4 block structure.
- I could see no blocking or banding in 2x to 3x crops, including around the lamp glow.
- Relay frames are not comparable, because the camera x differs by about 3 px between runs.
- Mobile ETC2/ASTC was **not rendered**, so it is unverified and needs a device check.
- The imported S3TC mid plate is about 2.1 MB, against 8.3 MB as raw RGBA8 (estimated arithmetic).

### Caveats
- The ideal Lanczos panel is composited over the already-rendered frame, so its edge fringe is an artefact of how I built it.
- Shimmer while the characters move was not measured, because all evidence is stills.
- Nobody has played any variant by hand.

All worktrees I created were removed. The main checkout and `wt-game` were not touched.

Does the shader bias of -0.5 cause visible shimmer while Rowan and WOLF walk or the camera pans? Only stills were captured, and nobody played the route by hand.

lv1.summary:
Track C1 (level design). I audited the committed game branch 934f1b2 (codex/game-presentation). I read the room code and rendered 22 fresh stills at a 1920x937 window, which Godot drew into a 1665x937 frame with side bars because the aspect is kept. The stills cover the start, middle and end of each room at play zoom 1.35, plus whole-room overviews at zoom 1.0. I also reviewed the existing stills and checked the advice against cited level-design sources. Nobody played the build by hand, so none of this validates feel.

The main finding is that the levels don't feel good yet for structural reasons, not because of the art. Each room is a single 960 px strip on one floor line at y 440. The camera shows 74% of the room at once (711 of 960 px) and can only pan 249 px. Stations sit evenly along the floor like cabinets in a row. The total walking across all three rooms is an estimated 13 to 14 s at the 190 px/s walk speed. You change rooms by pressing E at a station: the hard cut has no fade, no doorway and no walk-through.

The room gates and machines repeat each other's silhouettes. The Records exit hatch nearly duplicates the corridor sealed door (measured RMSE 0.17), and the Records purge queue nearly duplicates the corridor purge display (RMSE 0.15). The committed Junction reuses the corridor's background plates, tinted, with flat drawn placeholders. WOLF never uses the space differently from the engineer, and at two stations he parks on the engineer's exact spot: seam x 418 against valve x 420, and mirror x 520 against mirror x 520. In both stills he covers the person or the machine.

The approved next build (footsteps, room tone and reverb, acceleration and weight, breathing idles, the evidence case, one tool) fixes body feel. It does not fix space, transitions, camera framing, landmarks, depth or WOLF's use of the room. My recommendations focus on those, with costs, ranked by impact over cost.
lv1.findings_markdown:
## Scope and evidence labels
- **Build audited:** committed game branch `934f1b2` (codex/game-presentation), in a detached scratch worktree that is now removed. I made no repo edits.
- **The other job's junction work isn't in this audit:** its uncommitted junction art (painted props, its own far plate) exists only in `wt-game`. My fresh stills predate it. I mention it only through its own stills in `evidence/finish/junction-art-1/`.
- **Labels used below:**
  - **[measured]** read from code or captured metadata
  - **[rendered]** seen in Godot normal-renderer stills
  - **[estimated]** derived arithmetic
  - **[unverified]** craft judgment that nobody has playtested
- **Nothing here validates feel.** Nobody has played the route by hand.

## How the levels are built today
**[measured]**
- **Room size:** every room is one 960 px strip with one walkable floor at y 440. `RoomDepth.ROOM_WIDTH = 960`, and the actors are clamped to x 40–920 in `m0_actor.gd`.
- **Verbs:** the gameplay actions are `move_left`, `move_right`, `interact`, `choice_1` and `choice_2`. There is no vertical move. Walk speed is 190 px/s.
- **Camera:** `_update_gameplay_camera` clamps camera x to the engineer at a fixed y of 360, zoom 1.35 and smoothing 4. The visible width is 711 px, or 74% of the room. The camera can only travel between x 355.6 and 604.4, so 249 px. The capture metadata confirms that range.
- **Station x positions:**

| Room | Stations, left to right |
|---|---|
| Corridor | purge display 158, breaker 350, relay 605, door 780, safe point 876 |
| Records | purge queue 190, mirror port 520, exit 830 |
| Junction | breaker 200, vent 300, valve 420, door 452–508, rubble 540, alcove 556–584, mark 700, patrol 624–840, bolt 850, hatch 880 |

- **Room changes:**
  - In the corridor you press E at the safe point to save, then press E there again to enter Records.
  - In Records you press E at the exit to complete the chapter, then press E again to enter the Junction.
  - Both are hard camera cuts with no fade (comments in `_interact_checkpoint` and `_enter_junction`). The engineer reappears at x 128 or 120 next to the left wall. Records has no entry door drawn there.
- **Walking time [estimated]:**
  - Corridor critical path: about 716 px, or 3.8 s.
  - Records: about 702 px, or 3.7 s.
  - Junction including the retreat from the blast: about 1,150 px, or 6 s.
  - Total: about 13–14 s of walking for the whole chain. Measured capture walks agree: 430 px took 2.09 s of wall time.
- **Screen space taken by the HUD [measured]:** at 960x540, the top bar covers y 16–78, the context hint y 405–440 and the dialogue bar y 444–526. Only y 78–405 (61% of the height) is clear. The floor lands at screen y 378, so actors occupy roughly screen y 280–378. In every still the persistent dialogue card stays up.

## What the stills show
**[rendered]** Stills are in `audit/c1-out`.
- **The same layout grammar three times.** Every room is a pipe ceiling, three ceiling lamps, two red beacons, a wet floor, mirrored railing strips in the bottom corners, and three to five box-shaped machines standing on one line (`c-0-overview-sealed`, `r-0-overview`, `j-0-overview-sealed`).
  - The committed Junction is literally the corridor's background plates with a warmer tint (`junction_room.gd`). The lamps are in the same places.
  - Each room's gate is a tall red-slot slab: corridor door, Records exit and junction door. The Records exit is a near-copy of the corridor door (RMSE 0.17), and the Records purge queue is a near-copy of the corridor purge display (RMSE 0.15). Side by side: `audit/c1-out/cmp-props.png`.
- **The goal isn't visible at the start.** From the corridor start (camera x 355.6), the sealed door at x 780 and the safe point are off-screen. Nothing in the room leads the eye toward them; the HUD text does all the guiding.
- **Large empty floor between stations.** The corridor gaps between stations are 192, 255 and 271 px, and the Records gaps are 330 and 310 px. Those stretches have no interaction, no foreground layer and no change in light, so they are dead space rather than paced rest.
- **No depth layers to play on.** Actors and machines share one plane. The near layer is only edge railings, so nothing passes in front of the player mid-room, and there is no height change or backdrop activity.
- **WOLF covers the engineer or the machine.**
  - `WOLF_SEAM_X = 418` while `VALVE_X = 420`, so he stands where the engineer cranks. In `j-2-middle` he covers the engineer.
  - In Records his target is the mirror port x 520, so in `r-3-end` he sits in front of the machine. The manual-port route would stack both actors there.
- **The Junction is the best "level" in the chain.** It has a hazard zone, a blast to retreat from, a patrol lane, a refuge alcove and a drop mark, and the lane beat frames well (`j-2b-lane`, camera x 521.7, which keeps patrol 624–840 and the mark in view). But in the committed build:
  - Nine labeled things are packed into one strip.
  - The machines are flat drawn boxes over painted plates, which clash in style.
  - The lane uses the same flat floor as everything else.
  - The in-progress art in `evidence/finish/junction-art-1` (painted valve, blast door, tank arm, sentry) fixes much of the identity and density, but not the layout.
- **Capture caveat:** the dialogue text in my Records and Junction stills is stale because my driver loaded the room state directly instead of playing through the beats. That is not a game defect.

## Why it may not feel good: craft lens
These are **[unverified]** judgments backed by the sources at the end.
1. **There is no navigation problem for the space to solve.** Dan Taylor (GDC 2013) argues that good level design is fun to navigate, leads with light and geometry, and is driven by mechanics. Here the text panels do the leading and the floor asks nothing of the player.
2. **There is no rhythm or pacing curve.** Eric Chahi (GDC 2011, Another World) shaped tension "a little bit like a music score", mapped events on a pacing curve, and kept cinematic punctuation to brief moments. Here the corridor and Records follow the same calm, evenly spaced beat; only the Junction escalates.
3. **The rooms have no single idea that develops and then twists.** Hayashida (Super Mario 3D Land) teaches one mechanic per level, then develops it, twists it and lets the player show mastery (the kishōtenketsu structure), and Mark Brown's GMTK video popularised this. The corridor (routing power), Records (copying) and the Junction (pressure) each introduce an idea, but only the Junction twists one.
4. **The space has no prospect, refuge, compression or release.** Totten (*An Architectural Approach to Level Design*; GDC 2018) and Reeve's "Prospect and Refuge" tie pacing to open versus sheltered space. Every room has the same ceiling height and depth. The Junction alcove is a gameplay refuge, but it isn't built as an architectural one.
5. **Transitions break spatial continuity.** Pressing E at a save kiosk and cutting to a new room's left wall makes the chain read as separate menus rather than one facility. Playdead keeps very few elements per screen and places what the player will meet with intent. Carlsen's Limbo talk describes moving a bear trap onto a separate screen from a spider, and using a switch the player will most likely press by running past.
6. **The companion isn't using the space.** Ellie's buddy AI (Dyckhoff, GDC 2014) centres on positioning and staying out of the way. Elizabeth (Abercrombie, GDC 2014) is "both leader and follower". WOLF's 64 px follow gap and the two overlaps above work against both.
7. **Rooms lack memorable landmarks.** GMTK's Boss Keys analysis of Hollow Knight shows how distinct, memorable areas carry navigation. Here identical lamp modules and gate slabs make the three rooms hard to tell apart in memory.

## What the approved next build already covers
- **Body feel:** footsteps per surface, room tone and per-room reverb, acceleration and turn-around, the bob, lean and breathing pose layer, and look-at.
- **Reasons to look closer:** the evidence case, with the two starting traces plus pickups and wall screens.
- **One tool:** a hip tool that ratchets in the junction valve.

These improve physical presence and give players reasons to inspect things. They do not change:
- room width or layout
- the floor plane or depth
- how rooms connect
- the camera's composition
- landmarks
- WOLF's use of space
- set-piece staging

The recommendations below target those gaps.

## Recommendations by room
These are **[unverified]**; each needs a play pass before anyone claims it works.

**Corridor (teach and calm):**
- Make the sealed door a full-height landmark shutter that you can see from the start, or nudge the camera to look ahead toward it.
- Run a visible conduit from the breaker through the relay to the door, so cause and effect read in the space itself. The Junction already does this with its pipe run.
- Turn the door into a threshold: a narrow passage after it, then a release into the safe-point bay.
- Make the exit a doorway you walk through rather than a second E press at the save point.

**Records (investigation):**
- Give it its own gate art. The current hatch is a copy of the corridor door.
- Add one depth landmark, such as deep stacks with a lit aisle, a glass wall or a gantry.
- Spread the beats out so the walk between the queue and the mirror has a reason to exist, for example ambient reactions as you pass.
- Give WOLF a mirror spot that leaves the manual port clear, with a distinct scouting action such as nosing along the stacks.
- Carry the coolant/service line visibly toward the exit, so the next room is anticipated before you arrive.

**Junction (action set piece):**
- Land the in-progress art.
- Fix the WOLF/valve overlap: move his seam position to about x 390 or onto the door side.
- Build the alcove as a real recess, darker with overhead cover, so it reads as refuge.
- Persist the post-blast changes (debris, steam, light) and frame the lane beat on purpose.
- Make the hatch a doorway you walk into.

**Whole chain:**
- Give each room a distinct tempo and one landmark.
- Connect rooms by walking: a short fade or a camera carry-through at a doorway, then the engineer enters through a door and WOLF follows in or leads.
- Make room width a per-room value, so a room can be 1.3–2 screens when it has something to reveal.
- Add one height change per room that walking can handle (a ramp, stairs or catwalk). Light platforming is already the stated production direction.
- Add a foreground occluder layer mid-room.
- Let WOLF move through spaces the engineer can't, such as up on machinery or under pipes, to show his independence without giving the player control of him.
- Hide the dialogue card when no line is current, so the room has room to breathe.

recommendations.title: Walk-through room transitions instead of pressing E at a station and cutting
recommendations.detail: Corridor and Records: make the exit a real doorway or passage. Walking into its trigger (keeping USE as a fallback) starts a short fade of about 0.3–0.4 s, or a camera carry-through. Then spawn the engineer entering through a drawn door on the new room's left, with WOLF following through or leading. Keep the autosave on entry. In the corridor this also separates 'save' from 'leave', so pressing the safe point twice no longer changes rooms.
recommendations.impact: High. It turns three separate screens into one facility, gives a sense of progress, and removes the most menu-like moment in the chain.
recommendations.evidence: main.gd _interact_checkpoint (second USE calls enter_records, then _start_gameplay_camera with the comment 'cut the camera… instead of panning'). _enter_junction is also a hard cut. m0_state.gd enter_records/enter_junction spawn the engineer at x 128/120. Rendered still r-1-start shows no entry door.

recommendations.title: Stop WOLF covering the engineer and machines at stations
recommendations.detail: Move JunctionRoom.WOLF_SEAM_X off the valve, either to about x 390 with WOLF facing the door or to the door side. Move WOLF's Records target off the mirror port's x, about 40–60 px to one side, with a sniffing or inspecting pose there. Add a test that WOLF's target never falls within the engineer's interaction radius of an active station.
recommendations.impact: High for readability. Players can see the engineer cranking and the mirror machine, and WOLF reads as giving them space, which is the core of Ellie's buddy AI design.
recommendations.evidence: Measured: junction_room.gd WOLF_SEAM_X=418 vs VALVE_X=420; main.gd _wolf_target_x returns 520 for Records, which is the mirror port's x. Rendered: j-2-middle (WOLF covers the engineer at the valve) and r-3-end (WOLF in front of the mirror port).

recommendations.title: Give each room one landmark and its own gate silhouette
recommendations.detail: Replace the near-duplicate gates and terminals. The corridor gets a full-height lockdown shutter visible from the start. Records gets an archive-aisle hatch or lift. The Junction gets the blast door already in progress. Give Records its own purge terminal shape. Keep the lamp and beacon modules but break their even spacing, for example one dead lamp or one hero light over the goal.
recommendations.impact: High. Rooms become memorable and players can navigate by landmarks (Hollow Knight per GMTK Boss Keys; Taylor's principle of leading with light and geometry).
recommendations.evidence: Measured: ImageMagick RMSE corridor-sealed-door vs records-exit-hatch 0.172; corridor-purge-display vs records-purge-queue 0.155; side by side in audit/c1-out/cmp-props.png. junction_room.gd preloads corridor-far/mid/near plates tinted #b7a79c (committed). Rendered: c-0/r-0/j-0 overviews.

recommendations.title: Lead the eye with the space, not the HUD
recommendations.detail: Corridor: draw or paint a conduit linking breaker, relay and door, light the current objective with a hero lamp that changes with state, and add a small look-ahead so the camera leans toward the next unfinished station (an offset of about 60–90 px). Records: carry the service line visibly toward the exit. Keep the context hint, but make it confirm what the room already shows rather than replace it.
recommendations.impact: Medium-high. Navigation becomes 'fun to navigate' (Taylor), and the corridor's goal stops being off-screen at the start.
recommendations.evidence: Measured: at camera x 355.6 the view spans x 0–711, so the corridor door (780) and safe point (876) are off-screen at the start (c-1-start). _update_gameplay_camera has no look-ahead (clamp(human.x)). Junction already uses a drawn pipe run linking breaker, valve and door (j-0-overview-sealed).

recommendations.title: Add depth and one height change per room within the walk-only verb set
recommendations.detail: Add one walkable ramp, stairs or catwalk segment per room (CharacterBody2D with gravity already handles slopes). Put one mid-room foreground occluder on the near layer (pipe column, hanging chains, a doorway frame) that the actors pass behind. Add one background activity per room, such as a moving fan, a dripping leak or light behind glass. Use the space between stations as compression and release: a low ceiling, then a tall bay.
recommendations.impact: Medium-high. It removes the 'cabinets on a flat floor' read and supports the 2.5D direction. Prospect, refuge, compression and release give pacing without new mechanics (Totten; Reeve).
recommendations.evidence: Measured: one floor y 440 (RoomDepth.FLOOR_Y); the near layer is only mirrored edge strips (room_depth.gd near_strip_width, LeftEdge/RightEdge). Rendered: the overviews show identical railings in the bottom corners in all three rooms and no mid-room foreground.

recommendations.title: Make room width a per-room setting and use it for reveals

lv2.summary:
Track C2 (atmosphere and horror lens) for game branch commit 934f1b2. I rendered 33 windowed stills at 1600x900 (GL Compatibility, M1 Pro) and took pixel measurements from them. I also read the room, depth, sound and intro code and checked the craft points against cited sources. Nobody has played the route by hand, so none of this validates how the game feels.

The rooms look good in a still, but the measurements show why they don't feel tense yet:
- **All three rooms are lit the same way.** Each has mean luma 30–35 and about 30% near-black pixels. The left, middle and right thirds stay within about 10 luma of each other.
- **The lights never react to the story.** The Corridor and Records use the same rig: three lamps, two lockdown beacons and the same evenly timed flicker. The beacons keep pulsing even after WOLF says "It's quiet now."
- **The rooms barely move when the player stands still.** Over 2 s, only 2.7–3.1% of the room area changes in the Corridor and Records, and 0.45% in the Service Junction before the blast. The title screen changes 0.00%.
- **The Corridor and Records are silent.** Their only sounds are a few one-shots when you use a station; looping sound exists only in the Junction.
- **The Junction is a re-tinted Corridor.** It reuses the Corridor's art, with code-drawn vector machines on top.
- **The sentry doesn't read as a threat.** It is about the engineer's height (73 vs 72 px) and has no sight cone.
- **There are no transitions between places.** Rooms are entered by a hard camera cut. The title key art shows a different place from the game, and the engineer appears after the intro without an arrival beat.
- **The screen is busy.** About 27% of the first gameplay frame is covered by UI panels (estimated).

The recommendations below are ranked by cost and impact. Most of the quick wins are about making light, sound and motion follow game state; they stay out of the already-approved next build (footsteps, room tone, movement weight, breathing, evidence case, one tool) except to say how to stage it.
lv2.findings_markdown:
## Scope and evidence labels
- **Build:** game branch `codex/game-presentation` at `934f1b2`, in a detached audit worktree that has since been removed. The main checkout and `wt-game` were not touched.
- **Setup:** imported twice headless (16 errors on the first import, 0 on the second). Run windowed at 1600x900 with an isolated HOME, using my driver `atmos.gd` (title, intro, first gameplay frame, each room at 2–3 camera positions, and idle pairs taken 2 s apart).
- **What each label means here:**
  - **MEASURED:** pixel statistics computed from those rendered stills.
  - **RENDERED:** what is visible in the stills.
  - **CODE:** read in the source.
  - **ESTIMATED:** my approximations.
  - **UNVERIFIED:** anything about feel. Nobody has played this by hand.
- **Driver artifacts (not game bugs):**
  - The dialogue in the Records and Junction stills is stale because the driver sets state directly.
  - The first capture run quit silently after 18 shots; the rerun completed. I did not investigate why.
  - The FPS values in the shot JSON files are not performance evidence.

## 1. Tension curve across rooms: currently flat
- **Same light in every room (CODE).** `room_depth.gd` gives every room the same recipe:
  - 30 far and 12 near dust motes;
  - one haze band;
  - lamp flicker that dips to 70% about every 3 s on a fixed loop (`_flicker`);
  - beacons that pulse on a fixed 2.6 s sine.
- **Corridor and Records are near-identical rigs (CODE).** Both have three lamps, shafts on lamps 1 and 2, and two red beacons. The Junction only changes the lamp colour to amber and tints the plates `#b7a79c`.
- **Nothing in the rooms reacts to story state (CODE).** No lamp, beacon or haze changes with the breaker, relay, purge copy, blast or clear.
  - `grep` finds no lamp or beacon writes in `main.gd`.
  - The red `IntroAlarm` wash is cleared in `_finish_intro`.
  - The Director orders "Lock down maintenance", but nothing in the room shows a lockdown starting.
  - At the end of the Junction, WOLF's line "It's quiet now" plays while the beacons keep pulsing.
- **Brightness is flat across all rooms (MEASURED, luma 0–255):**

| Room | Mean luma | Median luma | Near-black pixels (luma below 16) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Corridor | 32–34 | 23–24 | 29–32% |
| Records | 33–35 | 22–24 | 31–33% |
| Junction | 30–31 | 20–22 | 28–34% |

  - The left, middle and right thirds of every frame are within about 10 luma of each other (for example, Corridor 31/40/30). Pools of light and dark gaps between them don't really exist.
  - The ceiling band is about as bright as the floor band (Corridor 32 vs 34).
- **Craft reference.** Valve's Left 4 Dead pacing alternates build-up, peak and relax. Evolve's designers put it as: "You need to have those peaks and valleys… You can't appreciate the action unless you have some inaction." Right now the route has no lighting valley and no lighting peak.

## 2. Light and darkness
- **The light reads as ambient, not motivated (RENDERED).** Every station sits in the same even blue-grey light. Lamps are painted plus additive glow. Nothing casts light onto the actors, and the actors never step into darkness.
- **WOLF is not a light source in the rooms (RENDERED, CODE).** His cyan body lights exist only as painted pixels. In the intro he is a dark silhouette behind a flat vector cage until a modulate tint; there is no glow on the wall or floor.
  - A companion who is also the light in the dark is a cheap, on-theme horror device that fits "WOLF is an independent companion".
- **The vignette is fixed and gentle (CODE).** `post_grade.gdshader` applies a fixed 0.42 vignette and a cold tint, never driven by tension.
- **Reference.** Darkwood's developers credit "light and field of view mechanics" plus "a heavy emphasis on sound and music design" for "a dense, creepy atmosphere" without jump scares.

## 3. Motion in the environment
**Idle motion (MEASURED).** UI is masked out; the figure is the share of room pixels whose colour changed by more than 6/255 over 2 s with the actors and camera still.

| Scene | Changed pixels |
|---|---|
| Title | 0.00% |
| Corridor | 3.13% |
| Records | 2.74% |
| Junction before the blast | 0.45% |
| Junction lane with the sentry patrolling | 0.70% |
| Corridor with visual effects off | 0.00% |

- **What moves (diff images).** Only the dust motes, the slow light-shaft skew and the beacon pulse.
- **What is missing.** No drips, steam leaks, fans, swaying cables, falling debris, flickering screens, rack LEDs, papers or vent shadows.
- **The action room is the stillest before its action (MEASURED).** The Junction steam and sparks run only off pressure state.
- **The actors don't animate (CODE).** `m0_actor.gd` slides the sprite with no walk or idle motion; pose and breathing are in the approved next build.

## 4. Scale, space and quiet stretches
- **Each room is about 1.35 screens wide (CODE).** Rooms are 960 world px; the gameplay view at zoom 1.35 is 711 px.
- **There are no empty stretches (CODE).** Stations are packed in:
  - Corridor stations at x about 190, 350, 592, 780 and 880;
  - Records stations at 190, 520 and 830;
  - Junction stations at 200, 300, 420, 480, 570, 850 and 880.

  Inside and Limbo use empty walking stretches to build anticipation. Here there is nowhere to just walk and listen.
- **The threat is no bigger than the hero (CODE).**
  - The sentry is 52 px wide and about 73 px tall; the engineer is about 72 px (1536 × 0.047).
  - Its "eye" is two 4 px squares, and there is no searchlight or sight cone, although `SIGHT_RANGE` is 180.
  - Little Nightmares' fear is credited to "the odd proportions of the 'enemies' and the way they move".
  - Alien: Isolation's director argued the threat "couldn't be scripted as this would evaporate tension". The sentry is systemic, which fits, but its presence is under-sold.
- **Rooms are joined by hard cuts (CODE).** `_interact_checkpoint` and `_enter_junction` say "cut the camera". Pressing USE at a door teleports you into the next room, with no doorway, transit space or sound bridge.

## 5. Sound and silence (what exists today)
- **Corridor and Records (CODE).** Only one-shots:
  - the breaker clank;
  - the relay clank and arc;
  - the intro boom;
  - the door-landing thud;
  - the Records arc.

  Long stretches are total digital silence, with no music and no bed under it. That is not designed near-silence: Limbo pairs near-silence with a "lively… muffled sound texture".
- **Junction (CODE).** Has loops: hiss and hum that follow the pressure gauge, a sentry servo, and a winch, plus growl, klaxon (played once at the valve) and booms.
- **The visual-effects switch also mutes all sound (CODE).** `sfx_bank.enabled = effects_enabled`; the approved build already plans to fix this.
- **Title (CODE, MEASURED).** No sound, and the image is fully static.

## 6. Environmental storytelling and lived-in detail
- **Corridor (RENDERED).** Clean wall and floor plates with stations lined up like a showroom, labelled in UI type.
  - There are no human traces: no cart, cup, notice, tools, tape, scuffs, or scratches by the cage.
  - The purge exists only as text on a display.
- **Records (RENDERED).** The most lived-in plate: server racks with amber LEDs, cross-braced columns and overhead cables. But the LEDs are static paint, and the "logs disappearing" stakes are never shown happening.
- **Junction (RENDERED, CODE).** Painted Corridor plates with code-drawn flat vector machines on top (pipe run, gauge, valve wheel, arm panel, alcove, tank labelled "COOLANT", sentry).
  - It reads as a diagram over a painting.
  - Labels clutter the frame; for example, "RELIEF VENT" is half-hidden behind WOLF.
- **Reference.** Smith and Worch's GDC 2010 "What Happened Here?" talk argues props, lighting and composition should let players infer past events ("subtext, which transforms simple scenes into something with a deeper meaning").

## 7. Title to first room: does it sell the place?
- **The title is fully static and silent (MEASURED: 0.00% change over 2 s).**
- **The key art shows a different place (RENDERED).** It has a city view, a bridge, warm and cold practical lights, and rain sheen. The game rooms have none of these.
- **New Game skips any sense of arrival (CODE).** It fades from black in 0.55 s straight into the containment two-shot at zoom 1.8. There is no establishing view of the facility.
- **The engineer is never introduced (CODE).** They first appear after the intro's fade to black (`human.show()` in `_finish_intro`), already standing beside WOLF. The arrival or meeting is not shown.
- **The intro cage is flat vector rectangles over the painterly wall (RENDERED).** WOLF inside reads as a dark blob until his tint changes.
- **There is no title sound at all.** That includes no transition sound into the intro.

## 8. UI load versus atmosphere (ESTIMATED from stills)
- About 27% of the 1600x900 frame is covered by opaque panels at the first gameplay frame (top card, tutorial prompt, context hint, dialogue bar, pause button), and about 18% in Records.
- Limbo's direction stripped UI to let imagination work. A HUD isn't wrong here (accessibility needs player-paced text), but the room never gets a moment without panels over it.

## How to stage the approved next build for atmosphere (no new scope)
- **Footsteps (per surface).** Vary the surface by state: wet concrete in the Corridor, dampened tile in Records, the vent grate and, after the blast, rubble in the Junction. A footstep on the grate becomes a tension cue near the vent.
- **Room tone and per-room reverb.**
  - Corridor: long concrete tail, plus a distant lockdown PA or klaxon once after the intro, then near-silence.
  - Records: the quietest, driest bed.
  - Junction: metallic. Let the tone duck about 1 s before the blast and the tank drop (valley before peak), then return thinner afterwards.
- **Breathing and pose layer.** Drive breathing from a tension value, such as sentry distance and pressure gauge, rather than time. Stillness plus breath is the quiet moment.
- **Evidence case.** Place examinable human traces (section 6) so props pull double duty. Item text stays Nathanial-approved.
- **One tool.** The ratchet at the Junction valve is a sound beat; give it a dry close-mic sound against the room's reverb.

recommendations.title: Make lights follow story state (a real tension curve)
recommendations.detail:
Add a small per-room 'mood' state to RoomDepth (lamp intensity, beacon on/off, haze alpha, vignette strength) and drive it from M0State:
- Corridor: intro ends, beacons start plus one PA or klaxon (the lockdown becomes real); breaker armed, a brief brownout then steady.
- Records: beacons off or one only, darker, pools at the two terminals (the quiet valley).
- Junction: lamps dim as the gauge rises (power draw), the seam lights the room, and after the blast the lane side stays darker.
- Cleared: beacons stop and haze settles, so 'It's quiet now' is true.
The vignette uniform can follow the same value.

perf.summary:
Track B (runtime GPU, CPU and RAM) was measured on main e2cccfe and on the branch at 16610a4 (codex/game-presentation HEAD when I started). One caveat applies to everything: the Mac's screen was locked and the display had been off since 00:46. A quiet window came at 03:23 (load 3.75, no other Godot running), and every run started with no other Godot process. Load still sat at 3.2 to 7.5 during runs, and one repeat ran at load 13.6; that one is flagged in the evidence.

**Desktop: no performance problem.** With V-Sync off and no cap, every state ran at 490 to 1,055 FPS. The worst p95 was 2.95 ms, at 1920x937 with effects on. That is more than five times the headroom of a 60 FPS frame (16.7 ms).
- **Effects cost:** about 0.3 to 0.4 ms per frame on the CPU side. Time to submit rendering went from 0.16 ms (main) to 0.29 to 0.50 ms (branch, effects on).
- **GPU cost:** at 1920x937 the GPU is busy for roughly 1 ms per frame on all three builds. At 960x540 it is too small to resolve. Godot's GPU timers return 0 on this renderer, and macOS's GPU reading covers the whole machine, so this is an estimate.
- **Memory:** the branch uses about 21 MB more texture memory than main (88 vs 67 MB at 960x540; 99 vs 79 MB at 1920x937) and about 27 MB more graphics memory. Process footprint is about 210 to 290 MB vs 175 to 225 MB on main.
- **Where the memory goes:** all 33 textures for all three rooms load at startup. The three character sprites take 25.8 MB of VRAM to draw figures about 100 px tall at 960x540.

**Shipped defaults (60 FPS cap plus V-Sync): measured 44 to 51 FPS, not 60, on main and branch alike.** An empty Godot scene showed the same thing: 49 FPS with a 60 cap, 87 FPS with a 120 cap, and V-Sync had no effect with the display off. So this is most likely the locked screen plus Godot's frame limiter, not the game. It is still unverified and needs a re-check on a display that is awake and unlocked.

**Startup:** launch to first title frame takes about 1.17 s on the branch vs about 0.93 s on main (medians of 6 runs each). The sound bank takes 37.7 to 38.3 ms to generate.

**Low-end Android: estimate only, never run on a device.** Roughly 95 to 105 MB of GPU memory, because 63 MB of sprites are stored uncompressed (RGBA8). Pixel load is about 4.5 full screens per frame with effects on vs about 2.2 with them off. Probably fine on Mali-G52 or Adreno 610 class phones, borderline on PowerVR GE8320 class at native resolution.

All runs were automated. Nothing here validates how the game feels, because nobody played it by hand. All audit worktrees were removed; the repository and wt-game were not touched.

**What's wrong (measured on rendered stills, Godot 4.7.2 Compatibility on an M1 Pro)**
- Main ships Rowan (1024x1536), WOLF (1902x1015) and the Director with mipmaps OFF and plain linear filtering.
- At the 960x540 default window, Rowan's 1478 px of art is drawn about 82 px tall. That is 18x shrinking; WOLF is 11.6x.
- Without mipmaps, each screen pixel reads only 4 of the hundreds of texels it covers, so outlines stair-step and break up.
- Control test: the branch art with mipmaps not sampled (plain LINEAR) brings back the same jaggies. So mipmaps are the cause and the fix, not the new art or the zoom. A skeptic independently reproduced the sharpness ratios.

**What the branch already does**
- `codex/game-presentation` turns on mipmaps with LINEAR_WITH_MIPMAPS. The jaggies are gone, but the characters come out soft.
- They look softer next to the props, which are only shrunk 2.45x to 3.35x. Correction: the props are painted renders, not pixel art; they look crisper because they are shrunk less.

**What does not work**
- The project setting `rendering/textures/default_filters/texture_mipmap_bias=-1` has no effect in this renderer. Rowan's pixels were identical with and without it (crop RMSE 0.00).

**Recommended fix (best of 9 variants in rendered stills, v3s)**
1. Keep mipmaps.
2. Shrink the art offline with Lanczos:
   - Rowan and Director: 1024x1536 to 256x384, scale 0.188.
   - WOLF: 1902x1015 to 761x406, scale 0.18325.
   - Feet and reflection maths stay the same (192 x 0.188 = 768 x 0.047).
3. Add one shared canvas_item shader that samples `texture(TEXTURE, UV, -0.5)` on the Human and Wolf BodySprites and IntroDirector. It multiplies by COLOR, so WOLF's tints still work.

This was the sharpest clean result at every size tested, and it cuts character VRAM from about 26 MB to about 2.7 MB (estimated). Required follow-up: the three manifest.json entries currently say "same 1024x1536 canvas", so the asset register must record the derived files and the new scales.

**Window size**
- At 960x540, Rowan is only 94 px tall on the branch, so no filter can show much detail.
- Opening at 1280x720 makes him 125 px (+33%). It is one default literal: `GameSettings.number(config, "video", "resolution", 0)` in main.gd.
- Players who already saved a setting keep it, and mobile is unaffected.

**Still unverified**
- Shimmer while walking or panning (stills only).
- 4K magnification: the 0.375 factor would be safer there.
- How any variant feels in play.

**Plates**
- Desktop S3TC compression measures about 37 dB PSNR, with no visible blocking in 2x to 3x crops.
- Corrections: the far plate has no alpha, so it is BC1 at about 1.0 MB; mid and near are BC3/DXT5 at about 2.0 and 0.5 MB.
- Mobile uses ETC2 only (high_quality=false), and nobody has rendered it on a device.

**Verdict: fine on this Mac, with lots of headroom (measured).**
- **Frame time:** the heaviest state (Service Junction, effects on, 1920 window) averages 2.4 ms with a 4.2 ms p99, about 14% of a 60 FPS frame.

- That the game holds 60 FPS with the display on and the window focused. The capped runs were throttled to about 49 FPS by the test conditions: screen locked, window never focused, and an empty control scene shows the same.

The rooms look good as stills, but they are built like a row of kiosks. Everything here is from code, measurements and rendered stills; nobody has played it, so the feel judgments are unverified.

**1. No space to explore (measured)**
- Every room is a single 960 px strip with one floor line at y 440. The only verbs are left, right and use.
- At zoom 1.35 the camera shows 711 px, which is 74% of the room. It can pan only 249 px.
- Walking the whole chain takes about 13–14 s (estimated).
- The stations sit evenly along the floor. The corridor goal (door at x 780, safe point at x 876) is off-screen at the start, and only the HUD text points you to it.

**2. Rooms are not connected (code, still true at 16610a4)**
- To leave a room you press USE twice at a station: once to save, once to leave. The camera then hard-cuts with no fade, and the engineer appears against the next room's left wall, where Records draws no door.
- The chain reads as three menus, not one facility.

**3. Flat tension curve (code, with corrected measurements)**
- The Corridor and Records use the same lighting rig: 3 lamps, 2 beacons, a fixed 2.6 s beacon pulse, and a looping flicker.
- Nothing in the lighting reacts to story state. The beacons keep pulsing after WOLF says "It's quiet now."
- Correction: with the UI masked out, the rooms do have local pools of light. The horizontal thirds are about 29/47/31 luma and the ceiling is darker than the floor (27 vs 43), so "evenly lit everywhere" was overstated. The rig being shared and unreactive still holds.
- Over about 3 s of idle, only 2.7–3.1% of the Corridor and Records frame changes (dust, light shafts, beacons). The title screen is completely static and silent.
- The Corridor and Records have only one-shot sounds when you use a station. Loops exist only in the Junction (code, read at 934f1b2).

**4. WOLF gets in the way (corrected root cause)**
- The follow rule keeps WOLF at `human.x - 64`, always on the engineer's left, but his body is about 110 world px long. So his head overlaps the engineer in every room whenever he stops.
- After scouting he walks back through the engineer (j-1-start: wolf_x 126, human_x 120).
- It is not the seam-versus-valve x positions, so moving WOLF_SEAM_X would not help.
- In Records he reads the mirror port at x 520 by design, but his sprite covers the machine (r-3-end).

**5. Rooms are hard to tell apart**
- The two purge terminals look nearly identical, and the Corridor door and Records hatch are the same family: a tall slab with a red slot (cmp-props.png). The RMSE figure did not prove near-copies; unrelated props score the same.
- Correction: at 16610a4 the Junction now has its own painted plates, props and sentry. The "re-tinted corridor" finding is out of date.

**6. The threat is under-sold**
- The new sentry is about 44 px tall, shorter than the roughly 70 px engineer.
- Its beam is drawn 34 px long while it actually detects at 180 px.

**What the approved next build covers, and what it doesn't**
- It already covers body feel: footsteps, room tone, weight, breathing, the evidence case and one tool.
- It does not change space, transitions, camera framing, landmarks, lighting state or WOLF's use of space. Those are what the lists below target.
